question: How does BSP actually buy companies?
html:
BSP buys theme-first: it studies a sector, then wins a banked process for an anchor acquisition and adds on from there (BSP acquisition methodology). Larger checks come from sponsor secondaries. Smaller ones come from founders or partners taking their first institutional capital.

Sector thesis comes first

  • Deal releases present each company as the result of a thesis studied in advance. Examples include over a year in electrical services before CET, and a watch on accounting before Smith + Howard (BSP acquisition methodology).
  • Since 2024 the filter has narrowed to essential services. Punctual Pros, Frontline and CET are non-discretionary. Fair Harbor is the only discretionary consumer bet (BSP acquisition methodology).

Two kinds of seller

Seller typePortfolio companiesPattern
Sponsor secondaryThomas Scientific (Carlyle), BPI (Svoboda), Frontline (BV)Larger checks. Outgoing sponsor often rolls a minority (Svoboda, BV).
Founder or partner ownerFair Harbor, Smith + Howard, Punctual Pros, CETSmaller checks. First institutional capital.

(BSP acquisition methodology; BSP firm profile)

Process and advisers

  • Six of seven anchor acquisitions had a named sell-side adviser. Punctual Pros went to "eight finalists," so BSP mostly wins auctions rather than proprietary deals (BSP acquisition methodology).
  • Berenson advised BSP on Thomas, BPI, Frontline and CET. Harris Williams advised on Punctual Pros and Frontline. Morrison Cohen or Greenberg Traurig was counsel on every deal (BSP acquisition methodology).
  • Structures vary:
  • Thomas used an Apollo/MidCap unitranche maturing in December 2027.
  • Fair Harbor is equity-only on public record.
  • Smith + Howard used an alternative practice structure (BSP acquisition methodology).

Capital and management

  • The main fund shows $335M sold on Form D (Apr 2025). A separate Frontline vehicle raised $136.95M in Dec 2024 (BSP firm profile).
  • Rival flagships run $0.9-2.1B. BSP's checks therefore lean on co-invest and operating credibility (Private-equity landscape). The $50-250M check size is unverified.
  • Inherited CEOs in secondaries are replaced at about 13-15 months: Simmons to Haas at Thomas, Naidoo to Britt at Frontline. Founder CEOs stay, including Sean Taylor, Matt Buckwalter and John Duquette Jr. (BSP acquisition methodology).

Add-ons and limits

  • BSP states 23 add-ons; 21 are identified by name (BSP acquisition methodology).
  • The section describing the first add-on is cut off in the context. Add-on timing and pricing would need the full deal list.
  • All weights and patterns are inferences from public evidence (est.), not BSP's internal screening criteria.

Next actions

  • Pull the full 68-item deal list to measure time from anchor close to first add-on, by portfolio company.
  • Identify the two unnamed add-ons: one at Punctual Pros, one at Smith + Howard.
  • Check whether Punctual Pros add-ons are sourced proprietary or through auctions. Consolidators such as Sila, Gridiron and Watchtower are bidding in Central PA/NJ (Private-equity landscape).
  • Confirm the true fund size and check band from LP or Form D records before citing them externally.
